title: Low-Input Hi-C Sequencing Libraries from FACS-Isolated Mitotic Cells
author: Nichols, Salataj, et al.

steps.title: Configure sorter for purity
steps.instruction: Set up the BD FACSAria III with a 130 µm nozzle, enable four‑way purity mode, and attach a refrigerated collection‑tube holder to keep sorted samples cold.

steps.title: QC and select laser
steps.instruction: Run Accudrop quality controls, then select the GFP channel laser 488‑530/30 (or the laser matching the fluorophore used).

steps.title: Adjust channel voltages
steps.instruction: Using unstained cells, asynchronous stained cells, and nocodazole‑treated stained cells, set FSC, SSC, and GFP voltages; typical settings for COLO320‑DM are FSC 410 V, SSC 210 V, GFP 200 V, with GFP displayed in logarithmic scale.

steps.title: Set sorting gates
steps.instruction: Create sequential gates to (1) exclude debris (FSC‑A vs SSC‑A), (2) select singlets (FSC‑A vs FSC‑H and SSC‑A vs SSC‑H), and (3) isolate high‑GFP mitotic cells; gently invert tubes 5× to homogenize and never vortex the sample.

steps.title: MPM2 antibody staining
steps.instruction: Perform fixation‑compatible staining of cells with anti‑MPM2 primary (1:500) and goat anti‑mouse Alexa Fluor 488 secondary (1:1000) on ice, followed by washes and resuspension in sorting buffer.

substeps.instruction: Spin cells at 400 ×g for 5 min at 4 °C; aspirate PBS.
Permeabilize on ice for 30 min with cold permeabilization buffer.
Spin 400 ×g 5 min at 4 °C; aspirate permeabilization buffer.
Wash twice in 0.2 % BSA wash buffer, spinning 400 ×g 5 min at 4 °C between washes.
Block in 1 % BSA for 1 h on ice, inverting periodically.
Spin 400 ×g 5 min at 4 °C; aspirate supernatant.
Prepare primary staining buffer: dilute anti‑MPM2 1:500 in blocking buffer (3 mL per 15 mL tube).
Resuspend cells in 3 mL primary buffer; incubate 1.5 h at 20‑25 °C on a shaker.
Spin 400 ×g 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Wash twice in 0.2 % BSA wash buffer (400 ×g 5 min at 4 °C each).
Prepare secondary buffer: dilute goat anti‑mouse Alexa Fluor 488 1:1000 in blocking buffer.
Incubate cells in 3 mL secondary buffer for 1 h at 20‑25 °C in the dark.
Spin 400 ×g 5 min at 4 °C; aspirate supernatant.
Wash twice with 0.2 % BSA wash buffer.
Resuspend in 2.5 mL sorting buffer; keep on ice.

steps.title: FACS sort mitotic cells
steps.instruction: Sort stained cells on the BD FACSAria III using the gates defined above, at 1,500‑3,000 events / s in four‑way purity mode, collecting ~10 000 cells for a purity check and the remainder into a 15 mL tube; keep all tubes on ice and add 2 mL ice‑cold 1 % BSA before collection.

substeps.instruction: Use unstained control to draw mitotic gates.
Between each sample, run water through the sorter for 1 min at maximum flow to wash the system.
Add 2 mL ice‑cold 1 % BSA to the collection tube and invert 5 times to coat the interior.
Sort at 1,500‑3,000 events / s, 4‑way purity, 130 µm nozzle.
Collect ~10 000 cells into a 5‑mL tube for post‑sort purity analysis.
Collect the remaining cells into a 15‑mL conical tube; keep on ice.
After sorting, re‑run the 5‑mL tube to assess purity (expected 99‑100 %).

steps.title: Post‑sort centrifugation
steps.instruction: Pellet sorted cells, remove supernatant gently, and resuspend in low‑binding tubes for downstream processing.

substeps.instruction: Spin sorted cells at 300 ×g for 10 min at 4 °C (increase to 2 500‑3 000 ×g if pellet is invisible; do not exceed 3 000 ×g).
Carefully remove supernatant with a serological pipette (avoid vacuum).
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL 1 % BSA and transfer to a DNA LoBind 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Count and aliquot cells
steps.instruction: Determine total cell number, then aliquot 300 000‑500 000 cells per tube, spin down, remove all buffer, snap‑freeze, and store at –80 °C.

substeps.instruction: Count cells using a hemocytometer or automated counter.
Aliquot 300 k‑500 k cells into separate tubes.
Spin each aliquot at 300 ×g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Remove all supernatant without disturbing the pellet (PBS/BSA must be fully removed).
Snap‑freeze pellets in liquid nitrogen.
Store at –80 °C (up to three weeks; longer not tested).

steps.title: Fragment DNA
steps.instruction: Adjust sample volume to ≤100 µL with Elution Buffer and sonicate on a Covaris E220 to obtain 200‑400 bp fragments; verify size on a TapeStation.

substeps.instruction: If needed, add Elution Buffer to bring volume to 100 µL (do not exceed).
Sonicate with Covaris E220: Peak Incident Power 175 W, Duty Cycle 10 %, Cycles per burst 5, Treatment time 50‑80 s.
Aim for an average fragment size of 200‑400 bp (check on TapeStation; desired 250‑350 bp).
Store fragmented DNA at –20 °C for up to 3 days.

steps.title: Size‑select DNA
steps.instruction: Perform two‑step bead‑based size selection to retain fragments 200‑600 bp.

substeps.instruction: Transfer fragmented DNA to a tube; add 60 µL DNA Purification Beads, mix, incubate RT 5 min.
Place on magnet until solution clears; transfer ~160 µL supernatant to a new tube.
Add 40 µL DNA Purification Beads to the supernatant, mix, incubate RT 5 min.
Place on magnet; discard supernatant.
While on magnet, add 200 µL 80 % ethanol, incubate RT 1 min; discard supernatant. Repeat ethanol wash once more.
Air‑dry beads on magnet for 1 min.
Remove from magnet, resuspend beads in 30 µL Elution Buffer, incubate RT 5 min.
Place on magnet, transfer clear supernatant to a new tube.
Quantify DNA with Qubit; record concentration.

steps.title: Enrich biotinylated fragments
steps.instruction: Capture biotin‑labeled ligation products with T1 magnetic beads, wash, and elute into water.

substeps.instruction: Vortex T1 beads to homogenize; add 12.5 µL beads per sample.
Wash beads three times with 200 µL Binding Buffer (mix 20×, vortex 5‑10 s, magnet 5 min, discard supernatant).
Transfer exactly 200 ng size‑selected DNA (or the entire amount if <200 ng) into a tube and bring volume to 30 µL with Elution Buffer if needed.
Add the washed 200 µL T1 beads in Binding Buffer to the DNA; mix and incubate RT 15 min.
Place on magnet; discard supernatant.
Wash beads twice with 200 µL Wash Buffer at 55 °C for 2 min (lid set to 85 °C); magnet and discard supernatant each time.
Resuspend beads in 50 µL nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: End‑repair and dA‑tailing
steps.instruction: Perform end‑repair and dA‑tailing on bead‑bound DNA using the Arima kit reagents.

substeps.instruction: Prepare End‑Repair/dA‑Tailing master mix per reaction: 16 µL End‑Repair‑A‑Tailing Buffer + 4 µL End‑Repair‑A‑Tailing Enzyme mix.
Add 20 µL master mix to each 50 µL bead‑bound library; mix well.
Thermal‑cycle: 20 °C 15 min → 72 °C 15 min → hold 4 °C.

steps.title: Ligate adapters
steps.instruction: Attach sequencing adapters to the end‑repaired DNA while still bound to beads.

substeps.instruction: Keep samples on ice; add 25 µL Ligation Master Mix (23 µL Ligase Buffer + 2 µL T4 DNA ligase) to each 70 µL bead‑bound library.
Add 5 µL Adapter Oligo Mix; mix gently.
Thermal‑cycle: 20 °C 30 min → hold 4 °C.
Place tubes on magnet; discard supernatant.
Wash beads with 200 µL Wash Buffer at 55 °C for 2 min (lid 85 °C); magnet and discard.
Resuspend beads in 34 µL nuclease‑free water; proceed to PCR.

steps.title: PCR amplify and index library
steps.instruction: Amplify adapter‑ligated DNA and add unique index primers using Herculase II polymerase.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PCR mix per reaction: 10 µL 5× Herculase II Buffer with dNTPs + 1 µL Herculase II Fusion DNA Polymerase + 0 µL water (total 11 µL).
Add 11 µL PCR mix to the 34 µL bead‑bound library.
Add 5 µL of the chosen unique Index Primer Pair (see index table).
Thermal‑cycle: 98 °C 2 min → (7‑9 cycles for 300‑500 k cells, 8‑10 for 500‑700 k, 10‑12 for ~1 M) 98 °C 30 s → 60 °C 30 s → 72 °C 1 min → final extension 72 °C 5 min → hold 4 °C.

steps.title: Purify amplified library
steps.instruction: Clean up PCR product with DNA Purification Beads and assess library quality.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL DNA Purification Beads to each 50 µL PCR product; mix and incubate RT 5 min.
Place on magnet; discard supernatant.
Wash beads twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol (1 min each), then air‑dry beads on magnet for 3‑5 min.
Resuspend beads in 15 µL nuclease‑free water; incubate RT 5 min.
Place on magnet; transfer clear supernatant (purified library) to a fresh tube.
Quantify library with Qubit (1 µL).
Run an aliquot on a gel or TapeStation to verify size distribution (expected 250‑600 bp, peak ~400 bp).

description: Mitosis is a period of profound structural reorganization, when chromosomes condense, transcription largely ceases, and genome-wide interactions are extensively remodeled.2,3,4,5 Many fundamental questions remain about how the condensed mitotic state influences genome architecture and long-range contacts, and whether these changes carry functional consequences for cell division and subsequent interphase organization. Hi-C sequencing enables the study of three-dimensional (3D) genome organization, but most published protocols require large input cell numbers, which can be challenging when working with rare populations such as mitotic cells.6 Isolating a pure mitotic population is essential to address these questions and prevent background asynchronous signal in downstream Hi-C sequencing analyses, yet doing so in a cost- and time-efficient manner has remained a barrier, especially for slow-growing or difficult-to-synchronize lines. The traditional method of mitotic shake-off can lead to contamination of mitotic samples with asynchronously growing cells, complicating downstream Hi-C analyses.7 An ideal approach overcomes these challenges by enabling high-purity mitotic isolation from relatively small cultures, broadening access to mitotic Hi-C for studies of chromosome dynamics, genome stability, and cell cycle regulation.
